item.title: After GOP's brutal midterms, ‘Chuck Norris of Florida politics’ tells party to 'get up and fight'
item.description: Republican Florida Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, dubbed the "Chuck Norris of Florida politics" by Ron DeSantis, says the GOP must rise like warriors.
item.content:encoded:
When an insurgent's bullet shattered his arm in combat, Republican Florida Lt. Gov. Jay Collins did not wait around for an evacuation team; the Green Beret performed emergency surgery on himself to save the limb.

After the midterms that Gov. Ron DeSantis called a "near extinction-level" event for Republicans, Collins sees a national GOP lying bloodied on the field. He advises his battered and beaten party to show the same refusal to die, and get up like a warrior.

"Where we go from here is up to us as a Republican Party," Collins, dubbed the "Chuck Norris of Florida politics" by DeSantis, told Fox News Digital in an interview just days after the midterm "bloodbath."

"This can be a definitive death blow if we allow it to be, but I believe in what we stand for." he continued. "I believe in our Constitution. I believe in our founding fathers' vision. I believe that God blessed this nation. I think we have to knuckle down, learn, apply this, and we have come out with a relentless dedication and fury to focus on what matters: To lead our state, to lead our country, and be what we need to be for the American people. That is what we should choose to do."

"Hard times happen. Warriors, leaders get up and fight. That's what we have to do now."

DESANTIS CALLS GOP MIDTERM LOSSES 'EXTINCTION-LEVEL EVENT' — AND EXPLAINS WHY FLORIDA SURVIVED

The metaphor is not subtle. It is a road map, set forth by DeSantis' two four-year terms – the last year of which was supplemented by Collins as his No. 2.

HUGH HEWITT: THE GOP IS WOUNDED, NOT DEAD — BUT RECOVERY HAS TO START NOW

Collins said his home state's recent history of going from a purple state to a GOP stronghold is an example the rest of the country can follow.

"Florida's been the road map," he said. "I think we've been what I call the conservative proving grounds. I think that it's time for many here in Florida to use our voice and to be out there and help our party get back on their feet. Be resilient. Yeah, man, you got popped. You got hurt. Get back up, dust it off, and let's go lead. Let's learn."

While congressional Republicans scramble to assign blame for a devastating cycle of national losses – including the loss of Texas to Democrats – Florida has positioned itself as the country’s preeminent conservative fortress, now the largest red state on the 2028 map.

"Losing sucks, winning is awesome: Let's get back to more winning," he said. "We've just got to figure out how we're going to do that, and that's achievable. I think Florida is a blueprint. I think we have a responsibility to lead."

DAVID MARCUS: HOW ASHLEY MOODY SURVIVED THE BLUE TSUNAMI AND EMERGED AS A GOP STAR

Under DeSantis, Florida shed its long-held "purple" swing-state identity to become the nation's largest, most disciplined red bastion. Collins looked back on how he pulled in the no party affiliated voters (NPAs), the valued middle that can flip races and states, in his state Senate race before being tapped to serve under DeSantis.

"Republicans showed up, but the NPAs showed up and they overwhelmingly did not align with Republicans," Collins said, admitting that even Florida's heavy Republican registered voter edge led to slim margins in the tough midterm environment. "What does that tell us? Well, the biggest gap we had was that we didn't spend enough time communicating to our NPAs."

Collins pointed back to how he won a Tampa race in a district "that is not a conservative juggernaut in terms of Florida," running against the Tampa mayor's mother-in-law.

"This was my very first race," he recalled. "We didn't talk to a single Republican out there. We only knocked NPA's and light D's, and we won by 10. What does that tell you? In a community like Tampa, I didn't hide from my views. I told people I'm conservative, I'm a Republican."

JASON CHAFFETZ: FIVE TIMELESS POLITICAL LESSONS THAT GOT LOST IN 2026

"What I realized is if you're honest with people, you agree on more than you don't, but you have got to be willing to step in there and have that conversation," he said. "And we did that over and over and again. And we built a base of people who trust us, because I don't play games."

"As a party, we need to go back to being the party that welcomes folks in – a little bit more of a big tent – but we have to stand on our conservative values," he added.

Collins is termed out of office along with DeSantis in January, but he will evaluate his future in the state or the national party apparatus. For now, he is committing to nothing and merely saying, "Stay tuned."

TREY GOWDY: THE MIDTERMS WERE A PAINFUL LESSON THAT REPUBLICANS CAN'T SKIP LEARNING

Regardless of candidate or party, Collins goes back to his military background and having risked his life and literally sacrificed limb for unity.

"I wore a flag on my shoulder every single day that I served in uniform," he said. "I wore the flag on my suit, really every single day that I was out there, serving in our state or serving our nation in any way that I could. We're the American people; we are blessed."

Once the party picks its 2028 candidate, Republicans need to be all-in against the opposition, Collins said.

"We have to row the boat," he said. "Sept. 11 was a big day in our life. Sept. 12 was incredible because we saw the power and the might of what America can be. When we rowed the boat, our enemy was fearful. They were on their heels because they saw an absolute juggernaut standing righteously to defend our people and our way of life. What our enemy fears, what other nations fear is Americans coming together."

TRUMP-BACKED BYRON DONALDS TO MAKE HISTORY AS FLORIDA’S FIRST BLACK GOVERNOR

"We have to come together and realize that our nation is blessed," he continued. "It will fall if we don't come together. But it won't happen if we don't start uniting and remind ourselves that this is America, we're allies, internal in our country, and we're going to make sure that it's the greatest country moving forward. America's worth fighting for."

"We need to focus on getting through this, the aftermath of this cycle, wrap it up, transition, and make sure that we understand exactly what happened," he concluded. "You know, when we started the war on terror, and I was a young soldier, we spent two years trying to fight the last war. It wasn't very great, to be honest with you.

"Let's not fight the last war. Let's understand the operational environment. Let's under our gaps. Our weaknesses and how we can clearly address those. And then we're going to have to move with a righteous fury."

item.title: Patrick Mahomes suffers apparent elbow injury on throwing arm but returns to face the New York Jets

item.title: George W Bush welcomes 27 veterans to his ranch for 16th annual Warrior Ride
item.description: George W. Bush welcomed 27 veterans to his Crawford, Texas, ranch for the 16th annual Warrior Ride honoring their service and recovery journeys.
item.content:encoded:
Former President George W. Bush welcomed 27 veterans to his ranch in Crawford, Texas, for his 16th annual Warrior Ride, an event honoring their service and recovery ahead of Veterans Day.

"These veterans have overcome a lot... but there's no self-pity. There's no, 'Please feel sorry for me,'" the 43rd president said on Friday.

"They serve as a great example of how to deal with life's difficulties and recover. I've watched a lot of them over the years go from darkness to light," he said. 

Bush's continued involvement with wounded veterans drew praise from his cousin, Fox News contributor Billy Bush, who emphasized on "The Sunday Briefing" that the former president's commitment to service members did not end when he left the White House.

"George W. Bush has never wavered," he said.

"The greatest responsibility of the office is deciding to send troops to war, and inevitably, some get hurt. And for George W., that doesn't end when you walk out of office. He's done it 16 years in a row. He's hopping on his bike and riding with the guys."

NEARLY 200 INJURED SERVICE MEMBERS COMPETE IN 2026 WARRIOR GAMES

Bush also cited his cousin's portraits of wounded warriors as another example of George W. Bush's continued dedication to veterans.

GEORGE BUSH WELCOMES TOP OFFICIALS TO HIS HOME STATE FOR 9/11 REMEMBRANCE ON 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF ATTACKS

"Character matters, and his artwork is about wounded warriors. He has really, really lived it all the way through. So hats off to the old man."

Billy Bush also joked about seeing his 80-year-old cousin back on a bicycle.

"I'm a little nervous seeing him at 80 years old on there. Here he goes. Keep it on the flats, man."

item.title: Social media horrified by Dave Chappelle’s sick ‘joke’ about Charlie Kirk’s murder
item.description: Circulating video from Dave Chappelle's Madison Square Garden show captures him saying he does "feel better" after the assassination of Charlie Kirk.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian Dave Chappelle said he feels "better" following the assassination of Turning Point USA (TPUSA) founder Charlie Kirk during a stand-up performance in New York City on Friday night, provoking outrage across social media.

Despite rules barring cell phones from the Madison Square Garden show, a video circulating on social media shows Chappelle appearing to make the remarks during his "Karmageddon" tour stop in New York City.

"I feel f----- up saying this. It’s scary being a public speaker. And I mean, look, ever since that guy, Charlie Kirk, got murdered, and I shouldn’t say this publicly, but, I feel better."

'SNL' WEEKEND UPDATE ANCHOR CALLS REPUBLICANS SLURS, MOCKS CHARLIE KIRK IN STAND-UP SPECIAL

"I know I shouldn’t say that, but it’s just a feeling. I didn’t ask to feel this way," Chappelle said. He then described his unexpected high spirits in the aftermath of Kirk's killing.

"I just be driving around like, ‘Why am I in such a good mood? Oh!'" Chapelle continued on Friday.

TPUSA pointed Fox News Digital to Erika Kirk's statement on X, in which she wrote that treating the destruction of human life as a punchline is "disgusting."

"A culture that laughs at assassination is one of profound moral decay. It threatens the very foundation of our country and the principles that hold our democracy together. You do not have to agree with someone’s politics to recognize the value of their life. This should not be so hard," she continued.

"Shame, shame, shame on Chappelle," Elon Musk posted.

Benny Johnson, host of "The Benny Show" podcast, called Chappelle's remarks "sick," while political commentator Meghan McCain asked, "What the h--- is wrong with Dave Chappelle?!"

Former communications director to former Vice President Mike Pence Katie Miller tagged Live Nation, the entertainment behemoth that sold tickets for Chapelle's tour, on X and asked, "Is this something we agree with?"

Journalist Piers Morgan wrote that Chappelle's comments were "especially egregious given that Chappelle himself survived an attack on stage in 2022." 

Many on X pointed out that Charlie Kirk himself posted in support of Chappelle after the comedian was attacked. Kirk wrote that refusing to charge the comedian's assailant sent "a clear message that public acts of political violence are justifiable." The man who attacked Chappelle was ultimately charged with four misdemeanors.

Kirk was murdered at a TPUSA event at Utah Valley University in Orem on September 10, 2025.

A trial date for Tyler Robinson, 23, the alleged shooter, has not yet been set.

PETE DAVIDSON SPARKS BACKLASH AFTER EXPLICIT JOKE ABOUT SLAIN CHARLIE KIRK DURING NETFLIX ROAST

Robinson has pleaded ⁠not guilty to all seven charges filed against him. His attorneys are seeking to block cameras from an upcoming hearing.

Chappelle has received backlash for his edgier jokes over the years, including jokes about transgender people. 

Pushback against part of his stand-up show "The Closer," released on Netflix in 2021, led to a small group of Netflix employees staging a walkout in protest. 

Kirk's murder has been the subject of multiple comedians' sets, including, Pete Davidson, who faced backlash after an explicit joke during Netflix’s "The Roast of Kevin Hart" at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles. 

"Tony reminds me of Charlie Kirk in that he’s definitely been on camera letting a guy unload in his throat," Davidson said during the roast. 

"Saturday Night Live" "Weekend Update" co-anchor Michael Che also joked about Kirk's killing during his Netflix special, "Michael Che: Shot in Minnesota."

"I feel like Erika Kirk on this stage. That’s no disrespect to the Kirks, by the way," Che said. 

Che said he didn't know who Charlie Kirk was before the activist was killed, joking that he initially thought people were talking about "the dude from Star Trek."

Fox News Digital reached out to Chapelle's team and Madison Square Garden for comment but did not immediately hear back.

item.title: Forget prunes: Popular green fruit shows promise for constipation relief
item.description: A review of 33 studies links eating two green kiwis daily for four weeks to more regular bowel movements in people with constipation or IBS-C.
item.content:encoded:
Eating two green kiwis a day could help people struggling with constipation, a new review suggests.

The research, published in the journal Food, Nutrition and Health, looked at 33 previous studies and reports on kiwifruit and digestive health.

Eating two fresh green kiwis a day for about four weeks was linked to more regular bowel movements, less straining and better digestive comfort in people with constipation or irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C).

COMMON KITCHEN STAPLE MAY HELP RELIEVE MILD CONSTIPATION, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS

In one international trial included in the review, people with constipation had about 1.5 more complete bowel movements per week, while those with IBS-C had about 1.7 more per week. Both groups also reported improved digestive comfort.

The new review suggests there may be several reasons kiwi helps with constipation.

Its fiber can add bulk and hold water in stool, while the fruit's natural water and sorbitol may help make stool easier to pass. Researchers said the benefit likely comes from several parts of the whole fruit working together rather than one component alone.

Kiwi was not necessarily more effective than other constipation treatments.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

One U.S. trial included in the review found that green kiwi, psyllium fiber and prunes all helped improve chronic constipation. Kiwi was associated with fewer side effects and was well-tolerated by many participants.

The evidence is strongest for fresh green kiwi, the researchers noted. There is less research on gold kiwi, powders and extracts, so those forms should not be assumed to have the same effect.

Jason Heiselman, a New York-based certified nutritionist and professional chef at Hungryroot in New York City, previously told Fox News Digital that kiwi is an easy fruit to work into a person's diet.

"It feels like a no-brainer to include a few slices with any meal," said Heiselman, who was not involved in the new review.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Kiwi contains fiber along with a natural enzyme called actinidin, which can help with digestion, the nutritionist noted.

"Pairing kiwi with some good fat sources, like seeds, nuts or full-fat dairy, allows your body to absorb more nutrients," he said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

For people who do not want to eat kiwi on its own, the fruit can also work in savory meals, according to Heiselman. "Raw kiwi slices often make their way to my dinner table," he said.

Heiselman said he pairs the fruit with salty cheeses, toasted pistachios and shaved red onion, and has also used kiwi as the base for chutneys and relishes.

There were some limitations to the findings.

The paper reviewed previous research rather than conducting a new clinical trial, and the studies differed in the people involved, the types and amounts of kiwi consumed, and the results researchers measured.

Most of the research also looked at relatively short periods of time, so more studies are needed to determine whether the benefits continue long-term.

Fox News Digital reached out to the researchers for comment.

Andrea Margolis of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

item.title: MLW Saturday Night SuperFight: New era begins, Tessa Blanchard makes her debut and more
item.description: MLW Saturday Night SuperFight crowned Josh Bishop as world heavyweight champion after a bloody Last Man Standing match against Killer Kross.
item.content:encoded:
Major League Wrestling’s (MLW) first pay-per-view of the year embodied its tagline, "Choose Violence."

Saturday Night SuperFight featured major matches with well-known professional wrestlers giving it their all for one night. A few fresh faces also joined the fray with at least one putting the rest of the roster on notice.

The main event of the night also changed the landscape for the company as MLW looks ahead toward 2027.

Read below to see how Saturday Night SuperFight turned out at Cicero Stadium in Chicago.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Josh Bishop was confident when he told OutKick Dropkick he wasn’t going to fall into Killer Kross’ sleeperhold and he wasn’t going to stay down the necessary 10 seconds that would have lost him the Last Man Standing match and cost him the MLW World Heavyweight Championship.

He came through on his promises.

The hellish match ended with Bishop, who was already a bloody mess, baptizing a table with his blood and hitting Kross with Exit 187, sending him through the wood. Kross was trying to get back up and was using a chair to help himself get back on his two feet. Bishop made a heads-up play and kicked the chair from Kross’ grasp.

The referee counted to 10 and Bishop was crowned the new MLW world heavyweight champion.

Kross started the year as the champion when he won it at Battle Riot VIII. Bishop went through hell and back to get the belt around his waist and he has crowned himself the future of the company.

Bishop’s win over Kross may be the most talked-about moment of the night, but it was Austin Aries and Matt Riddle who stole the show.

Riddle challenged Aries for the MLW National Openweight Championship. From the jump, Aries and Riddle were locked in a bitter battle – almost literally. The first four minutes of the match the two were tied up and they danced all around the arena before breaking apart.

From there, Riddle tried everything to keep Aries down. He hit a cutter on Aries on top of the title belt that Aries was poised to use as a weapon while the referee was down. But Aries, a veteran in the game, grabbed the rope before the three-count was made.

Riddle was in disbelief as there were five minutes left in the 30-minute match. Aries tried to stall the best he could as the time ticked away. The two wrestlers exchanged punches and slaps before Riddle hit another cutter on Aries. But as Riddle made the cover, time expired.

The Chicago crowd pleaded for overtime. Aries got on the mic and said if Riddle wanted more time, the crowd wanted more time and MLW wanted more time, then he wasn’t going to deliver it for them. Riddle knocked out Aries with a backfist and paraded around with the title.

Aries won the match, but Riddle got his last lick in.

Tessa Blanchard made her highly anticipated MLW debut at Saturday Night SuperFight and faced off against a formidable opponent in Keyra. While it was in MLW’s house, Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL) was fully on display.

The bout featured fast-paced action. Keyra was rolling at one point. She didn’t want Blanchard to get any kind of momentum that was going to put her away.

Blanchard caught Keyra with a thrust kick and hit a DDT to put Keyra away. Blanchard made clear she was putting the rest of the MLW women’s division on notice.

Shotzi Blackheart is currently the MLW women’s world champion but there’s a whole host of women on the roster gunning for her. Blanchard is far from the only one but her momentum is building.

The rest of the roster includes Scarlett Bordeaux, Zamaya and Masha. But you never know who else is going to "choose violence."

Trevor Lee knew what he was doing when he challenged IWGP heavyweight champion Yota Tsuji for a match at Saturday Night SuperFight. He wanted to prove he was one of the top wrestlers in the business and can go punch-for-punch with the best in the world.

Lee put on a show, hitting multiple Collision Courses on Tsuji. But he would have needed to do a little bit more to keep one of the best Japanese pro wrestlers down. He went for a high-risk move from the top rope and got caught.

Tsuji speared Lee, only securing a two count. He moved to the corner and stalked Lee. He sprinted toward his opponent and nailed the Gene Blaster. Tsuji picked up the win after that.

Lee proved to the pro wrestling world he has what it takes to be in the ring with some of the best the sport has to offer. Saturday just wasn’t his night.

item.title: DAVID MARCUS: Where does the blue tsunami leave old school Dems like John Fetterman?
item.description: John Fetterman's moderate stance on Israel and immigration puts him at odds with the Democratic Party's ascendant progressive wing in the new Senate.
item.content:encoded:
On Tuesday night, the American people triggered a political earthquake by thrusting Democrats into power in both the House and Senate by overwhelming margins. The defeat has already left the GOP in a circular firing squad of recrimination, but Democrats, too, must now face their own party's new divisions.

That’s where Pennsylvania Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., comes in front and center.

Fetterman in recent years has replaced former Sens. Joe Manchin, of West Virginia, and Kyrsten Sinema, of Arizona, as the most vocal and pugnacious moderate on issues such as immigration enforcement, support for Israel and a refusal to shut down the government to achieve liberal policy wins.

MAVERICK DEMOCRAT SURGES WITH REPUBLICANS AS HIS OWN PARTY TURNS ON HIM, STOKING TALK OF GOP SWITCH

Fetterman's penchant for criticizing progressive shibboleths was one thing when Democrats toiled in the minority, but how will incoming Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and his leadership team deal with the Pennsylvania maverick now that they control the upper chamber?

It is possible that Schumer just waits Fetterman out. The latter is up for re-election in 2028 and currently, according to surveys, is more popular with Keystone State Republicans than with Democratic voters there, making his chances of retaining the seat, at least as a Democrat, rather remote.

CHUCK SCHUMER AFTER SWEEPING DEMOCRATIC MIDTERM VICTORIES: 'I'LL BE RE-ELECTED AS MAJORITY LEADER'

Fetterman, it should be noted, is not the only nominally moderate Democrat facing voters in a purple state in two years. There are also Patty Murray of Washington, Maggie Hassan of New Hampshire and Catherine Cortez Masto of Nevada. But one must ask: Will they be more afraid of a general election defeat from the right or a primary ouster from the left?

A year ago, Democrats had dreams of a Senate majority, but it wasn't quite the Senate majority they have wound up with. In Michigan, they expected a Haley Stevens or Mallory McMorrow, not an Abdul El-Sayed. In Maine, an Angie Craig, not a Troy Jackson. These avatars of the progressive wing of the party will be the celebrities of the next Congress.

MAJORITY OF AMERICANS BROADLY REJECT SOCIALIST IDEOLOGY EVEN AS FAR LEFT SURGES TO POWER

It is difficult to imagine this firebrand faction working hand in hand with a White House they flat-out accuse of fascism to pass bipartisan legislation. But just as hard-line MAGA senators have been frustrated by Senate Majority Leader John Thune's temperance on issues such as killing the filibuster, incoming leader Chuck Schumer may well wish to resist the resistance, so to speak.

In fact, establishment Democrats and media pundits have been quick to remind us all that the vast majority of Democrats serving at the Capitol are not of the socialist variety, even though the party's zeitgeist and primary wins such as those in Michigan and Maine are with them.

JOE MANCHIN WARNS DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE GAINING GROUND AS DEMOCRATS REMAIN SILENT

The good news for Democratic leadership is that the scale of the victories Tuesday gives them big enough margins — 80 or so seats in the House and four to six in the Senate — that the socialists should not be able to hold legislation hostage. But that doesn't mean they have to be quiet about it.

There are several issues where we can expect the ascendant far left of the Democratic Party to draw lines in the marble of the Capitol, chief among them support for Israel and funding for immigration enforcement. Schumer will likely have to bend the knee to these demands, but not John Fetterman.

As Republicans delve deep into their postmortems, assigning blame for defeat, Democrats are celebrating a kind of Easter. But the question is: What exactly is this resurrected political party? Are the socialists a flying buttress to the establishment Democrats, or are they, in fact, the body of the cathedral now?

Fetterman raised eyebrows at this year's GOP midterm convention in Dallas when he appeared via video to celebrate the other Pennsylvania senator, Republican Dave McCormick, leading some to believe that the sweatshirt-wearing contrarian could switch parties — something he has consistently told the media, including this columnist, that he will never do.

Democrats in leadership have insisted for months that there has not been a far-left takeover of the party of Jefferson and Jackson, but rather that there is simply a big tent. Well, we know the tent is big enough for the likes of California streamer and anti-Israel firebrand Hasan Piker, but is there room in it for John Fetterman?

There was a scenario in play on Tuesday in which Fetterman could have become the 51st Democratic senator and close to the most powerful man in Washington. That did not happen, but he remains the most distinctive voice in D.C.

Has the Democratic Party outgrown the likes of old-school John Fetterman? And if so, can Republicans use that fact to woo law-and-order, Israel-hawk Democratic voters over to their side? Or is Fetterman now just a man out of time, out of step and without a solid constituency of voters?

item.title: 'American Idol' star Justin Guarini endured dark spiral after Hollywood dream collapsed
item.description: "American Idol" alum Justin Guarini opens up about the dark spiral after RCA dropped him and how embracing failure led to Broadway, "Wicked" and a whole new identity.
item.content:encoded:
At the start of his career, Justin Guarini seemed to have it all: fame, fortune and a promising future in Hollywood.

After becoming the runner-up on the first season of "American Idol" in 2002, Guarini was thrust into the spotlight seemingly overnight. But when his Hollywood dream came crashing down, he found himself in a dark place that he would eventually come to view as one of his greatest blessings.

"I think it was one of the greatest things that could ever have happened to me," Guarini, who recently released his book, "Center Stage Confidence: How to Own Your Story and Command Any Room," told Fox News Digital. "Failure is the greatest teacher, one of the greatest teachers that we can have in any given situation because in that failure, you have one of two paths. You either give up or you keep going."

TAYLOR HICKS CREDITS FAITH AND BLUE-COLLAR BIRMINGHAM ROOTS FOR KEEPING HIM GROUNDED AFTER 'AMERICAN IDOL' WIN

However, this mindset didn't sink in until much later.

In his book, Guarini recalled the moment he learned he had been dropped by his record label, RCA, in 2003.

"I stared at the TV in shock as my entire world came crumbling down around my ears," Guarini, who said he learned the news during a "Weekend Update" segment on "Saturday Night Live," wrote in his book. "Every illusion of fame, fortune, and glory fell away in an instant — only to be replaced by the silence of loss. In that moment, the veil of my arrogance, my assumptions, and my entitlement were lifted away, and I saw my life for what it had become."

"I spent months playing my sad story on repeat," he added. "I lost weight, slept more and more, and became less and less like myself, and the people who loved me started to notice and worry. I was living the ghost of the life I had always dreamed of and burning money and time in equal and absurd measure."

'GOLDBERGS’ STAR JEFF GARLIN SAYS HE PLANNED TO TAKE HIS OWN LIFE AMID TURBULENT FINAL DAYS ON SITCOM

As the first runner-up in "Idol" history, Guarini believed his future in the entertainment industry was secure. But his early success proved difficult to sustain.

In 2003, he released his self-titled debut album and starred alongside Kelly Clarkson in the musical romantic comedy "From Justin to Kelly." While his album debuted in the top 20 on the Billboard 200 chart, the movie flopped, and criticism of his performance and appearance continued.

WATCH: 'AMERICAN IDOL' STAR JUSTIN GUARINI ENDURED DARK SPIRAL AFTER HOLLYWOOD DREAM COLLAPSED

As his career stalled, Guarini struggled to reconcile his newfound reality with the life he had envisioned.

KELLY CLARKSON WON’T LET HER KIDS WATCH ‘FROM JUSTIN TO KELLY’ AFTER BRUTAL ADMISSION ABOUT 2003 FILM

"There have been plenty of people who've given up and failed and found other things," Guarini told Fox News Digital. "That's really wonderful. But for me, that dark place of not wanting to get out of bed, not wanting to look at myself in the mirror, not wanting to go out and see anything, it just was a period of isolation. And it's very easy to do when you live behind a gate in an exclusive community."

Over time, Guarini began to change his outlook.

COUNTRY STAR GABBY BARRETT SAYS SHE 'SLEPT IN THE CAR' BEFORE 'AMERICAN IDOL' CHANGED HER LIFE

"I realized that there were still people celebrating me," he said. "I realized there was still something worth celebrating in my life. And it wasn't the vanity metrics of how many people voted for me or how many followers I would end up having or the amount of money I could make or blah, blah. It was just doing something and going back to something that I really truly loved."

For Guarini, that meant returning to the stage.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"For me, that came in the form of just going back out and getting on the stage and singing for people. And I would do it at everything from gala events to state fairs to wherever."

Those smaller performances eventually paved the way for a new chapter in his career.

After independently releasing his second album in 2005, Guarini found opportunities in television before making his Broadway debut in "Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown" in 2010.

He went on to appear in several Broadway productions, including "American Idiot," "Romeo and Juliet" and "Wicked." In 2015, he introduced audiences to another side of his talent when he began portraying Lil' Sweet, the flamboyant character featured in Diet Dr Pepper advertising campaigns.

Looking back, Guarini said his willingness to embrace failure rather than run from it ultimately led to opportunities he might never have experienced had his initial fame endured.

"So there was a cascading effect. So the bottom line was being willing to sit in that place of failure, of discontent, darkness, but continue to go and continue to just say, ‘Okay, how can I continue to move through this space of discomfort, learn about myself and keep going?’ And ultimately, that led to a massive amount of growth that I don't think would have happened had I just, you know, stayed famous."

Now, nearly 25 years after his "Idol" debut, Guarini said his successes and failures have taught him one thing: don't give up.

"And so, for me, it has been almost 25 years now of some awesome ups and downs, and every single time I go up and down and up and down, it's just a consistency again of staying in the game," he said.

"And so, finally, just staying in the game… because it doesn't matter if it's the media, it doesn't matter if it's entertainment, doesn't matter if it's business. This life in this world is cyclical and if you stay in the game, and you do good work, and you're kind to people, the opportunity always comes back around to you, and you'll be more prepared to take advantage of it when it does," he added.

item.title: Dunleavy calls Alaska voting system ‘very confusing’ as razor-thin Senate race frozen in time
item.description: Republican Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy calls ranked-choice voting "very confusing" as Mary Peltola leads Dan Sullivan by just 637 votes in Senate race.
item.content:encoded:
Republican Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy admits his own state's voting system is "very confusing," and warned that the close race between Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola and incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan will not be determined for days, if not weeks.

"It's very close, the numbers," Dunleavy told WABC Radio's "The Cats Roundtable" on Sunday, noting key dates for ballot dumps will be Friday, Nov. 13, and Wednesday, Nov. 18, when "another big batch of votes will come in."

"It's a slow system up here in Alaska," he admitted, acknowledging that "we've got quite an issue up here."

"A big batch of votes will come and that'll really determine, you know, who's going to have the lead."

ALASKA, MISSISSIPPI SENATE RACES SEPARATED BY RAZOR-THIN VOTE MARGINS

Peltola, currently with 48.17% support, leads by just 637 votes in Alaska's ranked-choice voting system that has not dropped any new vote tallies for days. Election Day was Tuesday, Nov. 3, and if no candidate gets 50% support as the No. 1 choice by Nov. 25, the results go to rounds of ranked-choice candidates on the second and third choices.

"It is very confusing," Dunleavy said. "That was also on the ballot, to actually repeal that voting scheme that was put in place here just a couple years ago, and so it's confusing, 100%."

ALASKA VOTER 'DISGUSTED' BY REPORTED 'DECOY DAN' PLOT SWITCHES FROM PELTOLA TO SULLIVAN

"No" votes against repealing ranked-choice voting lead very narrowly at 51.85%. That decision also remains too close to call a week after the polls closed.

"We're still in the process of bringing in votes and counting votes," Dunleavy said. "And we are in the midst of investigations as to determine if there was any wrongdoing, especially anything that might resemble perjury or, you know, a misrepresentation of individual's intent on how they wanted their candidacy to be placed on the ballot."

TRUMP ADMIN PUTS ALLEGED 'DECOY DAN' CONSPIRATORS ON NOTICE IN ALASKA ELECTION SPOILER PROBE

Dunleavy denounced what he called the "Decoy Dan" scheme that had Daniel J. Sullivan on the ballot in an alleged plot to siphon votes from the Republican incumbent.

The governor claimed the other Sullivan even allegedly tried to get on the general election ballot as Daniel S. Sullivan, using the middle initial of the incumbent instead of his own.

EX-ALASKA LAWMAKER DETAILS MYSTERY RECRUITER AS FBI, CONGRESS WIDEN 'DECOY DAN' SCRUTINY

"That kind of opened our eyes and we began an investigation back there, the Division of Elections did, to determine if this was a legitimate candidacy, and the Division of Elections at that time found that was not and did not put him on the ballot," Dunleavy said. "Then there was a court case and the Supreme Court in the end ruled against the Division of Elections in Alaska, and they must go on the ballot."

After a New York Times report tied potential knowledge of the "Decoy Dan" scheme on behalf of Peltola's campaign, Dunleavy reopened the investigation of wrongdoing.

"When The New York Times article came out, you know, we already knew a lot of what was happening there, but there was more revelations of that article," he said. "As a result of that, we began another investigation up here in Alaska, and the Department of Justice did the same, so you have this investigation going on right in the middle of an election."

item.title: Fast-food chain that once lit up American roads still missed decades later
item.description: Iconic fast-food chain The Red Barn once rivaled McDonald's with its Big Barney burger and barn-shaped buildings, but its 300 to 400 locations vanished by 1988.
item.content:encoded:
With its distinctive barn-shaped buildings and menu of burgers, fried chicken and other American classics, Red Barn was a pioneer in the fast-food industry.

Founded in 1961 by Don Six, Martin Levine and Jim Kirst, the chain grew to between 300 and 400 restaurants before its final locations closed in 1988, according to numerous sources. 

The first Red Barn opened in Ohio, although there's debate over whether Columbus or Springfield is its birthplace.

FAST-FOOD DRIVE-THRUS TOOK OVER AMERICAN MORNINGS FOR THESE KEY REASONS

"I think it's important to note that Ohio is actually a bit of an icon as a state when it comes to being the home of iconic fast-food brands," Capri Cafaro, the Ohio-based managing director of America the Bountiful Media, told Fox News Digital.

Wendy's, founded in Columbus, was one of the first restaurant chains to offer a drive-thru window, Cafaro noted. It also stood apart from the competition with its square hamburger patties.

The roast beef chain Arby's was also founded in Ohio, in Boardman.

The barn-shaped buildings of Red Barn restaurants were key identifiers of the brand, as were their comfortable, homey interiors, Cafaro said.

PIZZA HUT BRINGS BACK VINTAGE VIBES AS FRANCHISEES EMBRACE NOSTALGIC MAKEOVERS

"I think that there is something to be said about matching the aesthetic with the name and making that part of its marketing appeal," Cafaro said of the exteriors.

This "iconic material culture" was "pervasive in fast-food restaurants, not just in places like Red Barn, but places like Long John Silver's or, or even more iconically, Pizza Hut," Cafaro said, referencing the hut-style roofs of classic Pizza Hut restaurants.

The chain's menu consisted of comfort foods like hamburgers, fried chicken, fish sandwiches and more.

A double-decker burger called the Big Barney was similar to the Big Mac but predated the famous McDonald's item, which wasn't added to the national menu until 1968, according to the company's website.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Like McDonald's, Red Barn also used food-themed cartoon characters used as mascots, including Hamburger Hungry, Chicken Hungry and Big Fish Hungry, with "hungry" sometimes spelled "hungery," according to Tasting Table.

The brand also had a jingle: "When the hungries hit, hit the Red Barn."

Red Barn offered a self-serve salad bar, and some publications say it beat Wendy's to the punch. 

The Wendy's website, however, claims it was the first national chain to introduce salad bars, doing so in 1979.

At its peak, there were about 300 to 400 Red Barn locations across 19 U.S. states, Canada and Australia, according to Chowhound.

Many factors can influence a restaurant chain's survival or downfall, Cafaro noted. Red Barn filed for bankruptcy in 1986, according to Tasting Table.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The chain's last 22 locations were in New York, Ohio and Washington, D.C., with the final franchise lease expiring in 1988, Chowhound reported.

A few locations were reborn as independent restaurants with a similar feel to Red Barn, including one in Racine, Wisconsin, called The Farm, which permanently closed in 2020.

Although not in its original form, The Red Barn still lives on today, with other businesses occupying the recognizable barn-shaped buildings.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Fans of the chain share memories and nostalgic photos in a Facebook group called "I remember The Red Barn Restaurants," which has over 9,000 members.

Red Barn is "evocative of nostalgia and for people that grew up with it," Cafaro said.

But, she added, "it really also does speak to the power of food to evoke nostalgia and memories" and how people "equate food to maybe a happy place."

item.title: Fishing is big business, and FXR founder says the sport's growth is only getting started
item.description: Matt Robertson's record $1.25 million bass fishing win at The Champions highlights a booming industry now drawing 57 million American anglers.
item.content:encoded:
There was a time when catching a bass might earn you bragging rights, a fishing trophy or maybe a few bucks from your buddies. On Oct. 31, it earned one Kentucky angler $1.25 million.

Matt Robertson walked away from The Champions on Old Hickory Lake outside Nashville with the richest first-place payout in bass fishing history, capping a three-day tournament that featured a staggering $3.25 million purse and brought together some of the biggest names from Bassmaster and Major League Fishing.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

And if the event was any indication, the business of fishing has come a long way from the neighborhood pond.

According to the 2026 Special Report on Fishing from the American Sportfishing Association and Outdoor Industry Association, 57 million Americans went fishing at least once in 2025. That's up from 50.1 million in 2019.

Those numbers help explain why companies with roots outside the fishing industry have increasingly turned their attention to the water.

Take FXR, for example.

The Canadian company built its reputation making performance apparel for snowmobiling and motorsports. But founder Milt Reimer told OutKick OutDoors that he began recognizing fishing's potential roughly a decade ago, after discovering just how much overlap existed between his motorsports customers and the fishing community.

"We just started to connect through that, and then just realized, man, there is a lot of participation in Minnesota, especially," Reimer said.

Fishing, he explained, was already a summer passion for many of the same people who spent their winters on snowmobiles or their weekends riding dirt bikes.

That connection eventually led FXR into the fishing apparel business, where the company now sponsors several professional anglers including Robertson, Fisher Anaya and 2026 Bassmaster Angler of the Year Trey McKinney.

But for Reimer, the appeal of fishing extends well beyond the professional tournament circuit.

When asked what an event like The Champions says about the future of the sport, he summed it up pretty definitively: "It's real. It's here. It's in front of us."

Reimer described the adrenaline of a tournament boat launch and the sudden change of pace once anglers reach the water, where wind, current, sunshine and countless other variables determine whether they have a successful day.

It's that combination of competition and connection with the outdoors that he believes resonates with so many people.

And unlike many professional sports, fishing offers a particularly direct connection between the athletes competing at the highest level and the average person who just wants to wet a line after work.

"There is this massive connection both from the pro side to the regular, just weekend, evening fishermen," Reimer said. "We love that part of it, and we love the community it's building. It helps us to really connect across all our genres of motorsports that we're in, and this is the one core sport that's really generational and passed on in a big way. It really vibes with so many people."

That connection was on full display at The Champions, where 60 competitors from two rival professional circuits went head-to-head for a record-setting payday.

MATT ROBERTSON WINS RECORD $1.25 MILLION FISHING PRIZE, DECLARES 'TRAILER TRASH FOR LIFE'

For Reimer, who had three sponsored anglers in the top 15, the opportunity represented something special.

"It's hard to describe. I'm so jacked for the guys," he said before Saturday's championship round. "It's kind of a dream come true for them."

He also praised the tournament for creating a stage where anglers from the sport's two major circuits could compete against one another for a championship.

Robertson ultimately claimed the $1.25 million prize, while McKinney finished fourth and earned $200,000. Anaya finished seventh.

Events like The Champions illustrate just how far professional fishing has come. And with tens of millions of Americans already spending time on the water, there's no shortage of people who can appreciate what these anglers do for a living.

Whether someone is chasing a seven-figure paycheck on a national stage or simply hoping to catch dinner at the local lake, the appeal of fishing remains much the same.

The stakes might be different, but everybody's still waiting for that next bite.

item.title: Philip Rivers finalizing agreement to return to NC State as Wolfpack’s new head coach in remarkable move
item.description: Philip Rivers had already begun assembling a coaching staff before formally accepting the NC State job, sources say. His son Gunner enrolls in January.
item.content:encoded:
After N.C. State officials made the trek to Fairhope, Alabama earlier this week to formally meet with Philip Rivers, the former Wolfpack and NFL quarterback appears to be set to take the head coaching position at his alma mater.

The two sides are finalizing an agreement that is expected to be hammered out over the next 24 hours, sources told OutKick. The board of trustees at N.C. State have a meeting this coming week to approve the contract.

Conversations about Rivers taking the job in Raleigh had picked up after the school announced that Dave Doeren had been fired nearly two weeks ago.

Following a series of informal discussions with major donors about what it would take to make N.C. State competitive in the current era of college athletics, several Wolfpack boosters put a plan in motion to provide Rivers with the resources needed to hit the ground running.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

By the end of the week, all that was needed was pen to paper for the NC State alum.

But first, Rivers was going to finish his job as head coach of St. Michael Catholic in the Alabama high school football playoffs. His season came to an end on Friday night in Fairhope, as they lost in the opening round.

According to multiple sources, Rivers had already begun putting together a coaching and front office staff for when he formally accepted the job offer and signed a contract.

On Friday night, Rivers was coaching St. Michael Catholic in their Alabama high school playoff game, where his son Gunner also plays. In addition to the intrigue of coaching for the first time in college, Gunner is also committed to NC State and will enroll in January to start his own collegiate career.

One of the biggest points of emphasis for Rivers taking the job in Raleigh was that he would be given enough money to work with for a veteran coaching staff, given that this will be his first college job.

Sources tell OutKick that one of his contract asks was that he be given a big enough pool of money to attract assistant coaches with college experience that would be open to making a move to Raleigh.

Also, having the NIL resources outside of the revenue-sharing that schools participate in was a key part of negotiations for NC State athletic director Boo Corrigan landing the former NFL quarterback.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S JERRY JONES? TEXAS TECH BOOSTER CODY CAMPBELL DEMANDS RETURN ON INVESTMENT

From a fan perspective, it's obvious that the Wolfpack would be making a hire that would excite the base, and more importantly help sell tickets and also lead to an influx of donations needed to help fund rosters in the future.

This is seen as a win-win for both sides, given that this would obviously be an interesting splash around college football, especially in recruiting players who are familiar with the new head coach.

But there is also the obvious fact that players are going to go where the money leads them, though that's clearly not the case for every player.

Still, putting together a formidable roster that can compete in the ACC and subsequently for a spot in the upcoming expanded College Football Playoff is key to making sure this hire doesn’t turn into a dud over the next few years.

NICK SABAN SPEAKS TRUTH ON CFP EXPANSION: ‘THERE’S NOT 24 TEAMS’ THAT CAN WIN A NATIONAL TITLE, BUT MONEY WINS

We have seen countless coordinators in the college ranks receive their first shot at a head coaching job and watch it turn into chaos; just look at what is taking place with Tosh Lupoi at Cal this season, where general manager Ron Rivera is already sounding the alarms.

But, for a high school coach to be given an opportunity to start their collegiate career at the top, and especially at a school like NC State, goes to show you how much Wolfpack officials think about Rivers.

Now, the donors who have promised Rivers with the funds needed to compete will be tasked with making sure he can attack the transfer portal to add players to this NC State roster so that he can hit the ground running for the 2027 season.

This will be an interesting situation to watch unfold over the next few months, with NC State fans expecting this team to once again start competing for ACC titles on a yearly basis.

Welcome to college football, Philip Rivers.

item.title: The week of the backup QB in the NFL kicks off as Sanders, Milton, Minshew, Lock, and Wentz start
item.description: Five NFL backup quarterbacks start in Week 9, with Shedeur Sanders, Carson Wentz, and Drew Lock all stepping in for playoff-contending teams.
item.content:encoded:
It is the week of the backup quarterback around the NFL and by the time we're done, we could come to understand why the quarterback-driven league is, for some teams, a backup-quarterback-driven week.

Five backup quarterbacks are starting for their teams in Week 9, with three of those players thrust into the starting job on teams with playoff expectations.

MINNESOTA VIKINGS' SOFT BENCHING OF KYLER MURRAY LEADS TO CARSON WENTZ TAKING OVER AS NEW STARTING QB

This is the week Shedeur Sanders starts for Deshaun Watson with the Cleveland Browns, Drew Lock starts instead of Sam Darnold for the Seattle Seahawks, Carson Wentz starts for Kyler Murray with the Minnesota Vikings – all playing on teams in thick of a playoff hunt.

The situation is probably different for the Arizona Cardinals, who are starting Gardner Minshew, and the Philadelphia Eagles, who are turning to Joe Milton because both those teams are currently outside the playoff picture and indeed under .500.

So here's the breakdown of five new starters and what is at stake:

Minshew's last start before this week was Oct. 6, 2024, with the Raiders, and unlike most of the others in this group, he has already been given a chance to extend his tenure beyond this game.

EAGLES' JALEN HURTS PLACED ON INJURED RESERVE AFTER SUPERFICIAL BLOOD CLOT FOUND IN HIS CALF AREA

This will be Milton’s first NFL start, and while the Eagles have not committed beyond this game, Hurts’ season-ending injury gives Milton a legitimate opportunity to keep the job if he plays well.

Lock’s most recent start was Sept. 20 against Arizona, when he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns. Darnold is expected to reclaim the job when healthy.

Sanders last started an NFL regular season game on Jan. 4, 2026, in the Browns’ 20-18 victory over Cincinnati, the seventh of his 2025 rookie season.

item.title: Two female deer throwdown in a backyard as the they appear to be protecting their young
item.description: Viral video captures two female deer fighting on their hind legs, throwing hooves like boxers while their fawns watch the intense backyard clash.
item.content:encoded:
Deer facing off with one another and settling matters physically isn't reserved for just the bucks during rutting season. Female deer will throw down too, especially if they feel the need to protect their young.

Back in September, this was on display in an amateur photographer's backyard. She heard noises coming from the yard and when she looked out of her window she saw two does going at it.

She grabbed her phone and captured a viral video. They weren't cracking skulls like the males do when they tangle antlers, they were on their hind legs using their front hooves to deliver blows.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

These ladies were absolutely letting them fly with combinations that a boxer would be proud of.

"This happened in my yard yesterday evening," the woman who recorded the action wrote. "I was upstairs when I heard this noise outside like thumping, bumping and thrashing. My window was open so I ran towards it and saw these two deer fighting. Both were females protecting their young ones I think."

She added, "First time I have witnessed that. WOW! I immediately ran for my cell and started to video it through my mesh screen so hope it’s okay to view. The wildlife I see in my yard. Always thrilling."

YOUNG BUCK GETS RAGDOLLED AND TOSSED IN THE AIR DURING BATTLE WITH LARGER BUCK CAUGHT ON TRAIL CAM

A mesh screen isn't ideal for recording video, but it doesn't interfere at all with this action. The two go at it as a couple of fawns look on.

After several exchanges, one of them decides they've had enough. A valiant effort by both of the deer.

They will live to fight another day, although one of them is going to enter their next scrap with a little more confidence than the other. That's life. You win some and you lose some.

item.title: Leavitt reveals what Republicans must do to survive politically after Trump leaves White House
item.description: Karoline Leavitt says the GOP must find a new leader who can connect with working Americans and rebuild Trump's America First political coalition.
item.content:encoded:
Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said Saturday that Republicans must find a new leader capable of connecting with working-class Americans and rebuilding President Donald Trump's political coalition once he leaves the White House.

"President Trump wasn't on the ballot in these midterms. He'll never be at the top of the ticket again, and I think we need somebody who is America first, who can really tap into the forgotten men and women that President Trump drew to the Republican Party in historic way from 2016 all the way through 2024," Leavitt said on "My View with Lara Trump"

"You need someone who can really get out, speak to people about their struggles, their challenges, relate to them and offer promise and hope," she added, acknowledging that Democrats successfully motivated voters during the midterm elections.

Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, capturing battleground Senate seats in Michigan, Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina, Maine and Minnesota while flipping key House seats in Virginia, Iowa and Nebraska.

MAGA VOTERS REVEAL WHO THEY WANT TO SEE LEAD GOP IN 2028

Leavitt urged Republicans to study their election losses and analyze individual races to determine how to correct course.

"I think that's something Democrats did well in this election, in the midterms, was they obviously inspired people to turn out to vote because they made the people feel like we're going to make your lives better," she said.

ELAINE PARKER: DEMOCRAT WIN IS A WAKE-UP CALL FOR REPUBLICANS, NOT A VOTE FOR SOCIALISM

"We need to do that again the same way, the same fashion President Trump did. It just has to be a new person at the top of the ticket."

Leavitt also reflected fondly on her time as White House press secretary, expressing gratitude for the experience. She said she has no plans to run for office, preferring to spend time at home with her young children.

"I'm so happy being with my kids. I have zero plans to run for office," she said. "I'm all set."

item.title: Bill Murray pours Guinness for fans at New York bar after admitting fame 'is not easy'
item.description: Bill Murray played bartender on Halloween night, pouring perfect pints of Guinness for cheering fans at a bar in Yonkers and posing for photos.
item.content:encoded:
Bill Murray was spotted enjoying Halloween in Yonkers, New York, where he interacted with fans while working behind the bar.

The 76-year-old actor and former "Saturday Night Live" star was photographed sitting with Rory Dolan, the owner of Rory Dolan's Restaurant & Bar, and showing off his bartending skills by pouring Guinness for customers.

The actor looked like a natural behind the bar as fans cheered when he poured a glass of Guinness.

"He had a bottle of wine, a very nice bottle of wine, and he also had, he was drinking some beer, but he did pour a pint of Guinness," Dolan told Fox News Digital. "Three-part pour, which is good to see him doing it. It wasn't his first time to do it!"

ACTOR BILL MURRAY STUNS TRUMP'S TOP ECONOMIC ADVISOR WITH BIZARRE QUESTION ON NEWS SHOW

According to Dolan, Murray arrived at the restaurant on his own. Murray kept it casual in a black outfit, with a navy blue button-up vest over a long-sleeved black shirt. In addition to serving drinks, Murray took time to pose for photos with other patrons at the bar.

"I think because he really was looking for the Irish culture," Dolan said. "He had been in Ireland doing this show. He has an excellent show out, but he was building on that energy, and he wanted to get behind the bar, pour a pint, and he wanted to know all about me and Rory Dolan's and whatever else. He was just very inquisitive, and he was very, very gracious to all, every one of the customers who went up and asked for photographs and spoke to them at length, and he was just, it was just great to have him."

Dolan also shared that the restaurant was celebrating another patron's 90th birthday the night Murray visited.

"The 90th birthday was that evening and then the crowd was in before the 90th birthday," Dolan said. "There was a big funeral, and they all came out to the bar, and it was just, the place was full and he was loving it."

Dolan said other celebrities, including Pierce Brosnan, have also visited the bar.

Murray got his big break when he was cast on "Saturday Night Live" in 1977, winning an Emmy for his work on the show's writing staff. He went on to receive an Academy Award nomination, seven Golden Globe nominations with one win, four Emmy nominations with two wins and a BAFTA Award.

In his new docuseries, "A Course Called Ireland," Murray discussed his relationship to fame and whether being a public figure makes him happy, answering, "In a word, no."

item.title: Michael Vick suggests play-call in waning moments of Norfolk State's dramatic defeat was ignored
item.description: Michael Vick says he called "victory formation," but Norfolk State ran a different play that led to a devastating fumble in the final seconds.
item.content:encoded:
November is the time of year when the college football season zeroes in on how the major teams from the top conferences perform with weeks to go before the final playoff rankings are announced.

On this Sunday, it’s worth checking in on what happened to Michael Vick’s Norfolk State Spartans over the weekend. The North Carolina Central Eagles pulled off a miraculous victory over Norfolk State in a Football Championship Subdivision (FCS) matchup.

The Eagles won in the final seconds of the game but Vick told reporters it likely could have all been avoided if someone was listening to him. The former Atlanta Falcons quarterback was getting ready to celebrate when everything went south.

North Carolina Central had no timeouts and Norfolk State had the ball with 1:34 to play on Saturday. All the Spartans had to do was run the clock out. Vick said he called for the victory formation, which would have been at least two kneel downs or a running play to take as much time off the clock as possible.

Instead, Norfolk State quarterback Deljay Bailey took a snap from the shotgun formation, ran to his left and fumbled the ball. North Carolina Central recovered the fumble and the offense marched down the field and scored to take a 29-28 lead after missing the two-point conversion.

Vick said he told his offense to do the very opposite.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I don’t know what happened at the end of the game," Vick said, via WTKR-TV. "I put my headset down. I called victory formation. All we had to do was take a knee, kneel the clock out. That’s just situational football. I don’t know what happened in regards to that. I looked up and we was running the ball, and then I seen the fumble. But my final instructions was victory formation. That’s when you kneel it out. And they had, I think, zero timeouts left and the game was over practically."

"Well, I put my headset down, and I took my headset off because all we had to do was just run it three times, or two times, or kneel it out," he continued. "That’s called victory. I don’t know what happened. A run play was called. I looked up, I seen us running the ball. I don’t know what happened. I really don’t. I don’t know what the play call was. I don’t know why we even ran that play."

A video of the final moments of the game showed the players meeting with offensive coordinator Brian Sheppard. Vick was around the huddle without a headset and casually walked to the meeting. The former NFL star said he definitely called for a "victory formation."

It’s unclear why there was a risky play called at that particular moment.

Norfolk State did get the ball back and got into field-goal range. But a 37-yard field goal was missed.

item.title: Memphis star Jayden Reid breaks down in tears after leading Tigers to win over VCU: 'God blessed me so much'
item.description: Jayden Reid broke down in tears during his postgame interview after hitting clutch free throws to lift Memphis over VCU in an emotional home debut.
item.content:encoded:
The college basketball season is just one week old, and while it may feel far too early to start tossing around the label of 'moments of the year,' it's hard to imagine Jayden Reid's postgame interview following Memphis' win over VCU on Saturday not standing the test of time.

Reid, who transferred from Northwestern to play for Penny Hardaway's squad this season, has been an absolute force for the Tigers through their first two games.

After scoring 26 points in the team's upset over Iowa State to begin the year, he followed that up with a 32-point performance in his home debut for the Tigers in their 89-88 victory over the Rams.

ILLINOIS BASKETBALL PLAYERS HAVE PRICELESS REACTION AFTER LEARNING CAITLIN CLARK WAS AT THEIR GAME

As the game's leading scorer who also hit two free throws with five seconds remaining to hand Memphis the win, Reid joined the Tigers' radio network on the floor for a postgame interview.

While he eventually answered a few questions about the contest, those came after he broke down in tears and expressed extreme gratitude for the opportunity.

"I'm just so thankful, I'm just thankful man," Reid said through the tears. "God blessed me so much to be in that position. I always prayed for this. I'm just thankful for God putting me in a great position coming to Memphis out of the [transfer] portal. I'm just so thankful for my coaches and my teammates; it's a big-time win at home."

There aren't many players who would show that sort of emotion after picking up a win over an unranked team in game two of the season, which makes the vulnerable moment that much better.

Reid, a Westbury, New York, native, began his college career at USF, where he played two seasons before transferring to Northwestern. He averaged 10 points and five rebounds per game for the Big Ten squad before entering the portal again and taking his talents to Memphis.

item.title: Pro-life pregnancy center expands mission to help patients embrace their God-given gender
item.description: By listening to the Holy Spirit, Heidi Matzke, executive director of the Alternatives Pregnancy Center, said her clinic helps women embrace the gender they were given by God.
item.content:encoded:
Helping a transgender man detransition to being a woman again is not something the pro-life, gospel-led Alternatives Pregnancy Center even notes on its website. 

But because it is a full-service women's health clinic with doctors who specialize in hormone therapy, it's simply something they do in order to give women the care they need to fully embrace their God-given gender.

It is all based on listening to the Holy Spirit, said executive director Heidi Matzke.

STUDY REVEALS UNEXPECTED HEALTH BENEFITS AFTER 5 MINUTES OF PRAYER

Based in Sacramento, California, Alternatives is one of hundreds of like-minded pregnancy help centers across the country. These venues may have different names, but they all work to help women with unplanned pregnancies. 

Still, years ago when Matzke took over, she knew she needed help — heavenly help.   

Matzke told Fox News, "When God called me into this ministry... I felt the Holy Spirit impress upon my heart back then, 'Heidi, you're right. You have no idea what you're doing, and that's why you'd better be face-down before me every single day. You better be fasting and praying.'"

She did fast. And she prayed and listened, she said. 

The result today is a pregnancy help center that is also a full-service health clinic for women. 

It wasn't long before another challenge came Matzke's way, involving listening to God. 

She asked the Holy Spirit to direct her very short talk at a church soon after launching the full-service clinic. The pastor gave her just two minutes.  

Matzke heard the Holy Spirit say to talk only about the women's health services the center offered and nothing else — not even the unplanned pregnancy help.

She did as directed. While the congregation received her respectfully and politely, Matzke said she felt a sense of defeat.

Then, between services, a man dressed as a woman came to her in the pews. 

It was just the two of them. 

He said the words that changed both their lives. 

He said to her, "What you don't know about me is that I'm biologically female, and I encountered Christ. The Holy Spirit has done work in my heart, and I am now trying to detransition. But my current doctors have basically abandoned me and I have nowhere to go."

That "man dressed as a woman" was Jessica Rose. Her story is all over the internet.

On that faith-filled day, Rose told Matzke she had been sobbing uncontrollably during Matzke's short presentation, as she had been praying that morning that God would provide her with free women's medical care.  

By listening to the Holy Spirit, Matzke became the angel in Jessica Rose's life. 

Her doctors had been eager to start her on hormones and surgery to remove her breasts after just a 30-minute consultation. 

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Now, in the pew, Matzke was the answer to spirit-leading prayer.

The women's heath clinic at that moment became more full-service than Heidi Matzke could ever imagine. 

It became a place where all women, meaning adult females, can be strengthened and shown to love themselves as they are in the light of the Gospel of Christ.

On an episode of the "Lighthouse Faith" podcast, Matzke talks about her encounter with Jessica Rose.

She also shares how a series of events strengthened her resolve to develop a full-service health clinic led by the Gospel — and how listening to the Holy Spirit brings healing to many more people than we could ever imagine.

item.title: Facebook recovery scams use fake FBI profiles
item.description: Facebook ads promising to recover stolen funds are targeting scam victims again, and Meta confirmed removing flagged accounts after investigation.
item.content:encoded:
You've already lost money to a scam. You're frustrated and probably wondering whether you'll ever see that money again. Then, while scrolling through Facebook, an advertisement appears promising to recover your stolen funds. Suddenly, there's a little hope. Maybe someone out there can actually help. Unfortunately, that moment of hope is exactly what scammers are trying to exploit.

One of our loyal CyberGuy followers, Patrick K, recently tipped us off to suspicious fraud recovery advertisements and profiles appearing on Facebook. He shared screenshots of what he was seeing and urged us to warn others.

His tip caught our attention, so we decided to dig deeper and contacted Meta about the suspicious accounts and advertisements. After reviewing the examples we provided, Meta confirmed to CyberGuy that it removed the flagged accounts and ads for violating its impersonation policies. The screenshots Patrick shared are especially concerning. One promotes stolen-asset recovery services. Another uses FBI-related imagery and claims to help people navigate the Internet Crime Complaint Center, better known as IC3. Together, they show how convincing these offers can appear.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

WHY IDENTITY THEFT COMES BACK FOR THE SAME PEOPLE

The first screenshot Patrick shared shows a Facebook advertisement displayed under the name Adam Molina. The promotional image features a smiling man in a business suit against a purple background. The graphic bears the name "DARKTRACER" and asks whether you've lost assets or funds to scammers. Below that message, the ad promotes services like recovering stolen assets and retrieving hacked cryptocurrency wallets. At the bottom, there's a Facebook Messenger button inviting people to send a message.

That's what concerns me. Someone who just lost thousands of dollars could see this advertisement and believe they've finally found a solution. After all, it looks like a company offering specialized assistance. And because it appears as a paid Facebook advertisement, some people may assume the advertiser has been thoroughly vetted.

The second screenshot Patrick sent us is even more troubling. It shows a Facebook page displaying the title "Director of Fraud Investigations" and the name Grace K. The cover image features the White House, the FBI's J. Edgar Hoover Building and cryptocurrency graphics. It also displays references to IC3 and the U.S. Department of Justice. The page description claims to help fraud victims navigate the IC3 reporting process. It even suggests that people who lost more than $4,000 may qualify for federal review. That claim appears on the page, but we found no support for such a dollar threshold in the FBI's published guidance.

It's a convincing presentation for someone desperately searching for help. The American flags and official-looking graphics create the impression that a federal agency may be involved. But here's what you need to know. The FBI says IC3 has no official social media presence. It never investigates crimes or recovers stolen money through Facebook Messenger or Telegram. That means any Facebook page claiming to represent IC3 should immediately raise suspicion, regardless of how official it looks. Meta's subsequent removal of the flagged accounts and advertisements reinforces those concerns.

After CyberGuy shared Patrick's screenshots with Meta, the company investigated and confirmed that it removed the flagged accounts and advertisements for violating its impersonation policies. Meta also provided broader details about its efforts to combat these schemes. According to the company, it removed more than 179 million accounts, Pages and Groups for misrepresenting identity during the first half of 2026. Most were removed before anyone reported them. Since 2025, Meta says it has also removed more than 17.3 million Facebook and Instagram accounts linked to criminal scam centers.

This problem isn't new to Meta. The company previously worked with cybersecurity researchers at Graphika to identify fraudulent websites impersonating the FBI's IC3 complaint center. The scammers promised to help victims recover stolen money, including cryptocurrency. Meta says it blocked the fraudulent websites and removed accounts connected to those operations. However, the examples Patrick discovered show how these impersonation schemes continue to reach Facebook users.

On July 20, 2026, the FBI issued an updated public warning about scammers impersonating IC3 investigators. According to the agency, criminals create fraudulent social media profiles that appear connected to the FBI. They then approach people who have already reported losing money to online scams. In one documented scheme, a victim realizes they've been defrauded and threatens to report the crime to the FBI. Later, someone pretending to be an FBI agent contacts the victim through Facebook Messenger. The conversation may move to Telegram, where the impersonator provides a link supposedly connected to the victim's IC3 complaint. That link may contain malicious code or collect additional financial information. Either way, the victim faces another potential loss.

The FBI also warns about AI-generated videos impersonating federal officials. Some of these videos direct victims to fraudulent websites designed to resemble the real IC3 complaint center. Once there, visitors may be asked to submit personal information under the impression they're dealing with federal investigators. And this type of impersonation extends well beyond Facebook. In a separate September 17, 2026, warning, the FBI reported nearly 61,000 complaints involving law enforcement or government impersonation scams between January 2025 and July 2026. Reported losses exceeded $1.6 billion. Those figures cover a broad range of government impersonation schemes, not Facebook recovery scams specifically. However, they show how costly impersonating official authorities has become.

SCAMMERS ARE COMING FOR YOUR MONEY. HERE’S THE ONE THING YOU MUST NEVER DO

There's a particularly cruel element to recovery fraud. The criminals approach people who may already be dealing with serious financial hardship. Some have lost retirement savings, while others have been tricked into sending cryptocurrency to someone they trusted. When an offer arrives promising to recover those funds, it's understandable why someone might want to believe it.

In August 2026, the Federal Trade Commission warned that recovery scammers sometimes purchase lists of people who previously lost money to fraud. They use those details to make their offers appear credible. For example, someone may contact you claiming they've located your stolen funds. They might even know approximately how much you lost. That information can make the person sound legitimate, especially when they claim to represent a government agency or law firm.

Eventually, the supposed recovery agent introduces a fee. They might call it a processing charge or claim the payment will release your recovered funds. But after you pay, the promised refund never arrives. In some cases, the scammer also collects enough personal information to attempt identity theft. We've previously covered the scripts criminals use in cryptocurrency scams, including fake recovery services that demand additional cryptocurrency payments.

A convincing advertisement or official-looking Facebook profile can fool someone who's searching for answers. Fortunately, there are warning signs you can look for before responding. Here's how to protect yourself.

Anyone claiming they can definitely retrieve stolen cryptocurrency or recover all your lost money deserves close scrutiny. Recovery depends on the circumstances, and no legitimate service can guarantee success. Be especially cautious when someone promises fast results.

The FTC warns that scammers often demand processing fees before supposedly releasing recovered funds. These payments may be described as taxes or administrative charges. However, the FBI says IC3 never charges victims to recover stolen money.

If someone on Facebook claims to work for IC3, don't engage. The FBI says IC3 has no official social media presence. Instead, type IC3.gov directly into your browser to verify information or submit a complaint.

Scammers may begin contacting you through Facebook Messenger before asking to continue on Telegram. The FBI specifically identified this behavior in IC3 impersonation cases. Be cautious when an unexpected contact pressures you to switch platforms.

Never share banking passwords or cryptocurrency wallet recovery phrases with someone advertising recovery services. Also, don't install remote-access software at the request of an unexpected contact. Doing so could give scammers access to your accounts or device.

Search for the company's name alongside terms such as "scam" or "complaint." Look for independently verifiable business information and a legitimate track record. Keep in mind that scammers can create fake testimonials and misleading websites to appear trustworthy.

THE BEST DEFENSE AGAINST HIGH-TECH AI SCAMS IS LOW-TECH SKEPTICISM, EXPERT WARNS

Strong antivirus software can help detect malicious websites, phishing links and harmful downloads associated with recovery scams. Choose protection with real-time threat detection and web security features. Keep it updated to help defend against emerging threats. However, antivirus software cannot prevent every scam, especially if you're tricked into sending money yourself.
